questions.q: Why would df.duplicated(subset=["customer_name"]) give a misleading answer on orders.csv?
options: customer_name has no repeated values in this dataset
It would flag legitimate repeat customers, like Dana Whitfield's 3 separate real orders, as if they were duplicate rows
duplicated() cannot accept a subset argument

questions.q: Why doesn't df.isna() catch order 1014's negative quantity (-1)?
options: isna() only works on string columns
-1 is a valid, non-null integer — isna() only detects missing values, not business-rule violations
Order 1014 doesn't exist in the dataset
quantity is stored as text, so isna() cannot check it
questions.explain: A negative quantity is a logic/validity problem, not a missing-value problem, so it needs its own explicit check.

questions.q: In the mask bad_qty = df["quantity"] < 0, what does df[~bad_qty] return?
options: Every row that does NOT have a negative quantity
The original DataFrame unchanged
Every row that DOES have a negative quantity
An empty DataFrame
questions.explain: The ~ operator inverts a boolean mask, flipping True to False and vice versa.
